crop.notes: Book pages: the full 'Tom Allen, England' biography page and the facing full-length photograph.

ocr.notes: Accurate except the Mace fight stakes, printed $5,000 (£1,000), transcribed as $3,000; 'Mississippi river' capitalisation and minor punctuation.

summary.suggested: Portrait Gallery of Pugilists of America profiled Tom Allen with a photograph and a record of his fights from 1861 in England to his 1876 loss to Joe Goss, noting he had settled in St. Louis.

metadata.notes: Book, Pugilistic Publishing Co.; the 1894 date is not shown on these pages and could not be checked. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Allen was born in Birmingham, England, in April 1840 (the index gives April 23, 1839)
Allen's first fight was a loss to Waggoner of Birmingham for $25 (£5) a side; he then lost to Young Gould and to Posh Price
Allen beat Bingley Rose of Nottingham in ten rounds (29 minutes) for $125 (£25) a side
Allen lost to Bob Smith, the 'Liverpool Black', in 2 hours 15 minutes, then beat Jack Parkinson in 20 minutes for $125 (£25) a side
Allen fought Posh Price a second time, 41 rounds in 2 hours 5 minutes; Price had himself arrested and the stakes went to Allen
Allen fought a 35-round draw (1 hour 52 minutes) with Joe Goss in Monmouthshire for $500 (£100) a side
Allen received forfeits of $250 (£50) each from Bill Thorpe, Peter Millard and Mike Cocklin
Allen came to America in July 1867
Allen's first American fight was a 43-round win over Bill Davis at Chateau Island, St. Louis
Charley Gallagher knocked Allen out in the second round, after three minutes, at Carroll Island near St. Louis
Allen fought Mike McCoole nine rounds on Foster's Island in the Mississippi for $1,000 (£200) a side; the crowd broke into the ring and the referee gave the decision to McCoole
Allen met Charley Gallagher again at Foster's Island; though Allen had him beaten in the 11th round (25 minutes), the referee decided for Gallagher
Jem Mace beat Allen in ten rounds (40 minutes) at Kennerville near New Orleans for $5,000 (£1,000) and the championship of the world
Allen beat Mike McCoole after 29 rounds (20 minutes) at Chateau Island, St. Louis, for $2,000 (£400)
Allen fought a draw with Ben Hogan, the reformed preacher-pugilist, near Council Bluffs

Allen's last fight was with Joe Goss in Kentucky for the championship of America and $5,000 (£1,000), fought in two rings in Kenton and Boone counties; Goss won on a foul after 21 rounds in 53 minutes
After the 1876 Goss fight Allen was arrested and put under bonds
Allen settled down in St. Louis, where he still lived

notes: A full fight record, so more facts than usual. Book prints 'Kent' for the first ring's county, read here as Kenton County. Birth year 1840 conflicts with the index (1839).
